key_insight: Detonation spraying parameters can be tuned to control titanium dioxide coating roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity, with optimal settings maximizing surface water repellency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides process–property guidance and predictive equations that can help engineers select spraying conditions for desired coating performance.
method: Varied detonation spraying process parameters (e.g., nozzle passage speed and spray distance).
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity/contact angle.
Fit empirical relationships to identify optimal conditions and predict surface characteristics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that roughness, thickness, and contact angle follow specific trends with process parameters, including inverse power-law and parabolic dependencies, and that optimal spraying conditions were determined from these data.
watch_item: The reported equations are empirically derived, so their applicability may be limited to similar materials, equipment, and process windows.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
